name: swapon
description: Enables swap space — a file or partition the kernel uses as overflow RAM.

flags.description: Enable a swap partition, e.g. swapon /dev/sda3.
Summary of swap usage (deprecated; prefer /proc/swaps or swapon --show).

examples.explanation: Creates a 2 GB swap file with safe permissions.
Formats the file as swap and enables it immediately.

examples.command: echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
examples.explanation: Makes the swap permanent across reboots.

examples.output:
NAME      TYPE  SIZE USED PRIO
/swapfile file    2G   0B   -2
examples.explanation: Confirms the swap is active and shows usage.

about: Swap extends RAM to disk: the kernel pages out cold memory when RAM runs low. Partition swap is slightly faster; file swap is flexible and resizable. The swappiness sysctl (vm.swappiness, default 60) controls how eagerly the kernel swaps — lower values favor RAM. On systems with hibernation, swap must be at least as large as RAM.
useCases: Add swap to small VPS instances.
Fix "out of memory" kills (OOM) with breathing room.
mistakes: Forgetting mkswap before swapon on a new file.
Creating swap on btrfs without the NODATACOW/ chattr +C handling — it corrupts or fails.
warnings: Swap on slow disk turns memory pressure into extreme slowness; monitor with free and vmstat.
